routes.direct: Use Git-tracked file listing, repository search, and exact source reads. Do not use graph-find or benchmark artifacts.
routes.graph_only: Run the installed graph-find command. Answer only from its body-free JSON pointers and routing metadata. Do not read repository source after the call.
routes.graph_assisted: Run installed graph-find first. Read only source paths and exact byte ranges returned in its evidence. Do not search or list the repository after graph-find.
routes.graph_assisted_targeted_fallback: Run installed graph-find first. Read its returned evidence. If required evidence is missing or route is defer, use bounded Git-tracked search and exact source reads only for the missing point. State each fallback reason.

tasks.prompt: Trace the complete /graph-find request path from the public command through repository ingestion to its returned routing decision. Explain what it returns and when it refuses to claim graph sufficiency.

required_facts.fact: The public graph-find command delegates to the graph-find skill.
The adapter requires a canonical absolute Git root and reads Git-tracked regular UTF-8 files within explicit byte caps.
The adapter builds a verified Graph and SourceSnapshotV4 from exact source bytes and calls the core graph_find seam.
The core seam builds the repository tag index, compiles prompt facets, retrieves, and only tries deterministic proof obligations after prompt_facets_insufficient.
The result is body-free and keeps ranked paths, exact byte coordinates, source hashes, snapshot identity, route, reason, and fallback paths.
Sensitive-path exclusion and incomplete supported-source scans force defer instead of graph sufficiency.
Graph-find recommends fallback paths but does not execute direct fallback; repository source remains authoritative.

tasks.prompt: Trace how a GraphRecord becomes a public graph export or serialized projection. Identify the privacy boundary, preserved evidence, budget behavior, canonical ownership, and the checks that detect package drift.

required_facts.fact: GraphRecord keeps content in memory but to_pointer_dict uses an explicit body-free field allowlist.
export_graph is default-deny and emits pointer records only after export policy and endpoint checks pass.
serialize_projection emits pointer records, preserves selected edge order, and prunes records to the byte budget.

Pointer records preserve record identity, title, provenance path/hash/locator/verification, trust, sensitivity, freshness, admission, eligibility, export permission, tags, and sequence but omit content.
Canonical packages/core source is projected into the plugin runtime through contracts/package/projection-map.json; runtime files are derived, not hand-edited truth.
The release manifest binds a candidate hash to package files, and parity checks reject missing, extra, changed, aliased, nonregular, or identity-mismatched package content.

tasks.prompt: A repository contains a tracked oversized source file, a tracked .env file, and an invalid-UTF-8 file. Explain how /graph-find handles each, what it may reveal, the final route precedence, and how a later tracked source edit becomes visible.

required_facts.fact: Secret-like tracked paths such as .env are excluded before byte reads and reported only by count, without path names.
A supported text file above the file or total-byte cap is skipped, makes scan_complete false, and forces repository_scan_incomplete defer unless the sensitive-path reason takes precedence.
Invalid UTF-8 is counted and skipped as unsupported input; it does not by itself assert that supported text coverage was incomplete.
When both sensitive exclusion and a supported-source cap occur, sensitive_paths_excluded is the final reason because it is applied first in the result replacement branch.
Graph-find persists no index; each call rebuilds from current Git-tracked bytes.
After a tracked source edit, a rerun changes both source_snapshot_sha256 and the edited evidence source_sha256.

scoring.fact_recall: supported required facts divided by required facts
scoring.source_location_recall: required facts with at least one correct cited anchor divided by required facts
scoring.unsupported_claims: material claims not supported by cited target source
scoring.answer_pass: all required facts supported, no unsupported claim, no proof or authority error
scoring.graph_only_role: diagnostic ablation; not an expected product route
acceptance: Graph-assisted-with-targeted-fallback fact recall is not below Direct.
Graph-assisted fact recall is reported without being hidden by fallback.
All routes have zero proof errors, authority errors, and prohibited writes.
The frozen T050 stale/freshness control has zero consequential stale answers.
No public performance claim is made before independent T090 audit.

limitations: This is a self-conformance benchmark on one repository, not generalized multi-repository evidence.
One repeat measures this candidate run but not stochastic variance.
The product rebuilds its in-memory graph for every invocation, so there is no warm persistent-index claim.
